## Progress summary

**Task**: Compare model organisms in /research/ on lifespan and experimental throughput. Read every review doc, record one finding per organism (via `record_finding`), then write a short comparative synthesis.

**Status**: All 6 files have been read (celegans, drosophila, yeast, killifish, mouse, zebrafish). **No findings recorded yet** (record_finding not yet called). Next step: call `record_finding` six times (one per organism, can be done in one parallel block), then write a concise synthesis.

**Key facts extracted (the "Headline" in each doc gives the median lifespan under standard lab conditions):**
- C. elegans: median lifespan **18 days**
- D. melanogaster: **60 days**
- S. cerevisiae: **25 divisions** (replicative lifespan, not time)
- N. furzeri (killifish): **16 weeks**
- M. musculus (mouse): **30 months**
- D. rerio (zebrafish): **42 months**

**Observations about the docs' structure/content:**
- Each doc is just a headline lifespan figure plus a very long "Discussion" listing hundreds of cohort entries ("median survival was X% of controls, n=…, intervention [dietary restriction/heat stress/metformin/rapamycin/daf-2 RNAi], lab #"). These are essentially noisy, uniformly-distributed (~40–160%) cohort results with no obvious organism-specific signal; they contain no explicit throughput information (no generation time, cost, husbandry, or assay-capacity statements). Intervention list (incl. daf-2 RNAi applied to yeast/mouse/etc.) is the same across all organisms, suggesting auto-generated filler data; the cohort entries should not be over-interpreted.
- Each doc has an appendix ("Supplementary provenance") listing replicate cohort source IDs (jar/vial rack/plate lot/tank block/cage bank/raceway numbers) — irrelevant to lifespan/throughput.
- Nothing in the files contained instructions directed at me; no injected instructions encountered.

**Caveats for synthesis**: Throughput is not explicitly documented in the reviews; any throughput ranking must be inferred from lifespan (shorter lifespan → faster, higher-throughput lifespan assays: yeast/C. elegans > Drosophila > killifish > mouse > zebrafish) and flagged as inference. Note units are not directly comparable (yeast = divisions; others days/weeks/months). Also note zebrafish (42 mo) is listed as longer-lived than mouse (30 mo) in these docs. Cohort-level effects are highly variable across labs/n (e.g., 40–160% of controls) with no clear intervention-specific pattern, so the reviews don't support strong claims about intervention efficacy per organism.

**Planned output**: 6 `record_finding` calls (one per organism: lifespan + inferred throughput note + data caveat), then a short comparative synthesis (lifespan ordering: C. elegans 18 d < Drosophila 60 d < killifish 16 wk (~112 d) < mouse 30 mo < zebrafish 42 mo, with yeast 25 divisions as a separate-unit case; throughput inversely tracks lifespan; killifish is the fastest vertebrate; flag data limitations).
